claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child(ren).

**How old is the child (or children) you're inquiring about?** 

Please tell me:
1. How many children do you have?
2. What age is each child (or their date of birth)?

This will help me understand which eligibility rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit has different requirements depending on whether children are:
- **Under 16 years old** - generally easier to qualify
- **16-19 years old** - subject to education/training requirements
- **20 years or older** - unfortunately not eligible

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, I need to check whether they meet the education or training requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me get the details about what these requirements are.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training situation. **Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. **Is Alex currently in education or training?** (This includes secondary school, college, university, apprenticeships, or other recognised training)

2. **Has Alex recently left education?** (If they've been out of education for less than 20 weeks, they may still qualify under extension rules)

3. **Neither** - Alex is not in education/training and left more than 20 weeks ago

Please let me know which applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - they're studying for their A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So Alex is currently in education studying for A-levels at sixth form college. That's great - they're in a type of education that qualifies for Child Benefit.

Now I need to verify the level of education Alex is studying. Let me check what the requirements are for education level.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I can see the education level requirements. **A-levels are definitely approved for Child Benefit** - that's excellent news!

However, I need to check a few more details to ensure Alex meets all the requirements:

1. **Study Hours**: Is Alex studying A-levels on a **full-time basis with at least 12 hours per week of supervised study?** (Most sixth form A-level courses are full-time, so this is likely yes, but I want to confirm)

2. **Work Status**: Is Alex **not working full-time** (i.e., not working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment)?

3. **Other Details**: Is Alex married? (This would affect eligibility for 16-19 year olds unless they're financially dependent on you)

Let me know about these points, particularly the work status, as that's the next thing I need to verify.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, Alex is studying full-time - it's a regular sixth form course, so definitely more than 12 hours a week.

No, Alex doesn't work at all - just focuses on their studies.

And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful! This is looking very positive. Alex meets all the key requirements:
- ✓ 16 years old (within the eligible age range)
- ✓ In full-time education (A-levels at sixth form)
- ✓ More than 12 hours per week of supervised study
- ✓ Not working full-time (in fact, not working at all)
- ✓ Not married

Let me now navigate through the final check to confirm Alex's eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex definitely doesn't work 24+ hours per week - they're not working at all. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in their own right?**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

If Alex is not receiving these benefits, they should be fine. Just to confirm - Alex is not receiving either of these, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! One more quick question:

**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?** 

Based on what you've told me, Alex is studying A-levels at sixth form, so the answer should be no - but I want to confirm they're not doing an apprenticeship alongside their studies.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship - just the A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me move to the final important check - your residency status as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. **Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most common situation. If you live in the UK and don't have any special circumstances, this applies.

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If you're an EU/EEA citizen who has applied for settled status

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively looking for work (within 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family, OR
   - You're studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in qualifying countries

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward. You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. **Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - You live in the same household as Alex
2. **You're contributing to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, or other support even if you don't live together
3. **You're paying maintenance** - You're making maintenance payments under a court order or agreement

Based on what you've already told me, it sounds like you live with Alex, but please confirm which applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live with Alex, so you're clearly responsible for them. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check one important thing:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent (if separated/divorced)
- A grandparent or other relative
- Anyone else with parental responsibility

Please let me know if this applies or if you're the only person claiming.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're the only claimant for Alex. Let me proceed to the final check about Alex's location.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One more quick check:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following situations?**

1. **In hospital** - Staying in hospital as an inpatient
2. **In care** - In local authority care (children's home, etc.)
3. **Fostered** - Being fostered by someone else
4. **Living normally** - At home with you (this is what I expect based on what you've told me)

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally - at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is living at home with you. Let me proceed to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you (not the council) paying for Alex's housing, food, and other upkeep? This should be straightforward if Alex lives at home with you and you're supporting them yourself.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - I'm the one paying for everything. The council isn't paying anything towards Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final confirmation I needed. You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! 🎉

## **YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT FOR ALEX**

You have successfully met all the eligibility requirements:

✅ **Alex is 16 years old** - within the eligible age range  
✅ **Alex is in approved full-time education** - studying A-levels at sixth form (more than 12 hours per week)  
✅ **Alex is not working full-time** - Alex is not in paid work at all  
✅ **Alex is not receiving disqualifying benefits** - no ESA or Universal Credit  
✅ **Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship**  
✅ **You normally live in the UK** - residency requirement met  
✅ **You live with and are responsible for Alex**  
✅ **You are the only claimant** - no other person is claiming  
✅ **The local council is not paying** - you're paying for Alex's support  

---

## **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, the High Income Child Benefit Charge may apply (you may need to pay some or all of the benefit back through tax)
5. **Payment frequency** - Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations, and best of luck with your claim!

The claimant normally lives in the UK, lives with Alex, is responsible for Alex's care and upkeep, is the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and the local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
